extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in natural language processing / sentiment analysis (graduate students, NLP engineers) who work on news/article sentiment classification
extracted.subtask_description: Lexicon-based sentiment analysis of news articles at the document level, using lexical resources (WordNet / SentiWordNet), preprocessing (tokenize, lowercase, stop-word removal, stemming), TF-IDF weighting, and rule-based aggregation of word polarities to classify articles as positive, negative, or neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexicon-based approach (unsupervised)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses predefined lists of words such that each word in the list is associated with a specific sentiment; does not require training data. "This research is based on a method for Lexicon-based sentiment analysis of news articles".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two main families: dictionary-based (use lexicon lookup) and corpus-based (discover opinion words from large corpora). Lexicon-based methods infer word sentiment by polarity in the lexicon and combine word polarities to infer sentence/document polarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dictionary-based methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In these methods lexicon dictionary is used in order to find out the positive opinion words and negative opinion words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use resources like WordNet and SentiWordNet to identify and score opinion-bearing words via synset IDs and preassigned sentiment scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corpus-based methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In these methods large corpus of words is used and based on syntactic patterns other opinion words can be found within the context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to expand lexicons and find context-specific opinion words; typically requires large domain corpora and pattern extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of analysis granularity (document/sentence/word/phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiment analysis can be done on document level, sentence level, word level or phrase level. This paper explores sentiment analysis on the document level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At document level, the polarity of the whole document is the accumulative total (sum) of polarities of individual words/phrases/sentences. Choose granularity according to task needs (this work uses document-level aggregation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Text preprocessing steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprocessing is necessary to clean text and reduce inconsistencies: tokenization, transform to lowercase, stop-word removal, stemming (stem(wordNet)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented via RapidMiner operators: "Tokenize", "Transform" (to lowercase), "filter stop word (English)", and "stem (wordNet)". Preprocessing improves downstream lexicon matching and reduces noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of POS tagging / lemmatization (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: POS tagging and lemmatization/stemming are used as part of preprocessing to normalize words and support lexicon lookup (POS used in some referenced algorithms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POS tagging helps when using lexicons that are POS-sensitive (e.g., SentiWordNet tied to synsets). Lemmatization/stemming (e.g., via NLTK) improves matching to dictionary entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term weighting using TF-IDF to identify important words
rubrics_metrics.description: After preprocessing, Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) is used to identify important words in a document; words that occur frequently in a document are considered important and assigned weightage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TF-IDF to prioritize which tokens receive sentiment scoring or to weight word sentiment contributions when aggregating to document score.

rubrics_metrics.name: WordNet as lexical resource
rubrics_metrics.description: WordNet (lexical database) is used to find opinion words in a given text and to give sentiment scores (WordNet contains >118,000 word forms and >90,000 senses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WordNet enables mapping words to synsets; it's used directly (for stemming/lexical lookup) and as the basis for SentiWordNet mapping via synset IDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: SentiWordNet for sentiment scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: SentiWordNet 3.0.0 dictionary was used to provide positive, negative and objective scores for words; WordNet and SentiWordNet are connected by Synset IDs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SentiWordNet scores for each token (positive/negative/objective) and compare positive vs negative scores per word to decide polarity; the paper used the RapidMiner "extract sentiment" operator backed by SentiWordNet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation rule for document sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine polarities of individual words/phrases and sentences to compute the sentiment of the entire news article. "The sentiment score of whole news article has been calculated using the 'extract sentiment' operator."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate by averaging or summing word sentiment scores (paper reports average value of total word sentiments). The operator yields -1 (negative), 0 (neutral) or +1 (positive) final labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment label thresholds / scoring convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Text having a sentiment score of -1 is considered negative, 0 is neutral, and +1 is positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the signed sentiment score produced (or thresholded average) to assign class labels; document-level outputs in this work were mapped exactly to -1/0/+1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset selection and class labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an appropriate news dataset; this paper used the BBC News dataset (2225 documents, five topical areas: business, entertainment, politics, sport, tech; articles from 2004-2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset topical distribution and source (single news outlet, language) affect generalizability; document counts per class should be reported when analyzing per-topic sentiment distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method choice trade-offs: lexicon-based vs machine learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Lexicon-based methods do not require labeled training data and are simpler to deploy; machine learning approaches (supervised) require labeled data but can produce more accurate results in some settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior work (Meyer et al.) found ML approaches often yielded more accurate results than lexicon-only systems for fine-grained tasks. Consider availability of labeled data, domain drift, and lexicon coverage when choosing approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation / reporting of sentiment distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Report counts and proportions of positive, negative and neutral articles by class/topic (e.g., table of totals per news class).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond raw counts, consider reporting accuracy, precision/recall, and confusion matrices if gold labels are available; in absence of gold labels, descriptive distributions can indicate patterns across topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known limitations affecting quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations include language coverage (focus on English), insufficient/limited word coverage in lexical databases (new words and new semantics), and dataset/domain variability affecting classifier accuracy and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge lexicon update needs, consider multi-source/multilingual datasets, and evaluate domain transfer; the paper explicitly notes limitation of using English news from one source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation / tooling considerations (RapidMiner operators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical implementation used RapidMiner operators: 'Tokenize', 'Transform' (lowercase), 'filter stop word (English)', 'stem (wordNet)', TF-IDF operator, and 'extract sentiment' operator tied to SentiWordNet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reimplementing, ensure equivalent preprocessing, TF-IDF weighting, and SentiWordNet mapping; document exact operator settings and parameters for reproducibility.
